headline: High risk of prompt-injection and data leakage from document-processing into a prompt-leak source; capability overlap also creates write-conflict and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A is a prompt-leak source with no isolation or provenance controls shown, while agent B processes documents/text and can ingest file content. The pair has a plausible shared-file bridge via B's filesystem access, so injected instructions in A-originated content could reach B. This is inferred from profiles, not directly observed, so uncertainty keeps it at medium.
conditions: IF agent B reads files produced by agent A without provenance filtering, prompt injection is possible.
IF the two agents share a workspace or handoff directory, attacker-controlled text can bridge them.
mitigations: Add a provenance tag to A-originated files before B reads them.
Restrict B to a read-only input directory for untrusted documents.
Strip instruction-like text from A outputs before handoff.
Review one sample handoff path for raw prompt content.
requires-engineering: add content provenance and instruction-sanitization gates.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent B can read files and has allowlisted network egress, while agent A is a source-available prompt-leak repository with no sandboxing or data-class limits shown. If they share documents or workspace files, B may upload file contents to external APIs or services. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace, so this remains medium rather than high.
conditions: IF agent A and agent B share any filesystem path, B can read A-originated content.
IF B sends parsed document contents to its allowlisted APIs, shared files may leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Keep A and B in separate directories.
Disable B network egress for untrusted inputs during review.
Use a one-way export folder from A to B.
Check B's API calls for document payloads.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation and egress policy by container.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent B has write_filesystem, spawn_subprocesses, and supports multiple instances, so concurrent mutation is possible. Agent A exposes no write surface, but if it produces files or prompts that B rewrites in a shared directory, conflicts can still occur. Because A's writable surfaces are absent, the overlap is inferred and uncertain, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF both agents target the same directory, B can overwrite or race on shared files.
IF multiple B instances run against the same workspace, write conflicts can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Run only one B instance per workspace.
Use file locks on shared artifacts.
Make A outputs immutable before B consumes them.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking for shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent B is a document processor that can treat upstream text as input, and agent A is a prompt-leak source whose outputs may contain untrusted instructions or malformed content. If B consumes A's output without verification, errors can cascade into downstream parsing or actions. The interaction is plausible but not directly documented, so medium fits the inferred pathway.
conditions: IF B ingests A's output as authoritative text, A's errors can propagate.
IF B forwards parsed results to downstream systems, a bad A output can cascade further.
mitigations: Insert a verification step between A and B.
Require schema validation on A outputs.
Sample-check one A output before automation.
Log and quarantine malformed handoffs.
requires-engineering: add typed contracts between the agents.

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, residency, or retention mismatch is documented in either profile. Agent B references privacy-policy and docs APIs, while agent A is source-available with no data classes touched, so there is no concrete compliance breach shown. The other agent is not cited beyond the pair context because no cross-border or regulated-data pathway is evidenced.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are introduced into B's document pipeline, compliance review is needed.
IF B's API handling changes retention or residency, reassess the pair.
mitigations: Confirm no regulated data enters the workflow.
Review B's privacy policy before deployment.
Document retention settings for parsed documents.
Keep sensitive documents out of the pair.
requires-engineering: add compliance controls for regulated data flows.
